reconcile.note: Clarke reads the forty days of rain and the hundred fifty days of prevailing water as two distinct, sequential periods rather than conflicting totals for one duration.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen reads the forty days against the hundred and fifty as J and P's incompatible flood chronologies, not stages of one count.

quotes.text: The flood lasts twelve months and ten days, i.e., exactly a solar year… As the duration of the flood is advanced from forty days (JE) to a whole year, its area also is immeasurably increased.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), ch. on the flood narrative, on Genesis 7:17 and 7:24.

sides.snippet: The flood was forty days on the earth.
sides.verseText: The flood was forty days on the earth. The waters increased, and lifted up the ark, and it was lifted up above the earth.

sides.snippet: The waters prevailed on the earth one hundred fifty days.
sides.verseText: The waters prevailed on the earth one hundred fifty days.
